criteria.criterion: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs builds a failed job (Failed outcome) that has a final reading and accepted corrections, and asserts earlier_attempt carries them in order and redacted.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff: `a_failed_job_carries_its_corrections_in_order_and_redacted` builds a job with a final reading, two corrections (the second contains a synthetic GitHub token) and a Failed outcome. It asserts that `failed` is set, checks the reading summary, that corrections[0] == "merge only when opted in", and that corrections[1] holds `[secret:github-pat]` and not the token. The test passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: A test covers a failed job that has corrections but no verification record, and one that is itself a retry, and asserts its corrections reach the EarlierAttempt.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff: `a_failed_job_without_a_verification_carries_its_corrections` sets verification = None and asserts corrections == ["keep it short"]. `a_failed_retry_carries_the_corrections_of_the_jobs_it_retried` builds failed job B as a retry of failed job A and checks the retry of B: it asserts the original request and corrections == [A's, B's]. Both passed when I ran them.

criteria.criterion: The reader brief for a failed earlier attempt lists the corrections under the existing corrections heading, with a briefs.rs test asserting this.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff: `reader_briefs_list_the_corrections_of_a_failed_earlier_attempt` sets failed: true and two corrections. It asserts "which failed" appears and that the heading "The corrections and answers the user gave" comes before "> merge only when opted in", which comes before "> keep it short". The test passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` from the repository root: all tests pass, including the new failed-job correction tests.
criteria.evidence: Every `test result` line in the `cargo test -q` output shows 0 failed. The athena-core run shows 57 passed and the athena-context run 23 passed, which include the new tests.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings. `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing, and because it ran after `&&` it succeeded.

findings.summary: Only the retry-chain test fails without the fix. The other two new reading tests probably pass on the base code too, so they lock in existing behaviour rather than reproduce the bug.
findings.evidence: On the base code, `carry(job)` already copied a single failed job's own corrections. The only code change is in `earlier_jobs` and its call site, which affects retry chains only. This is my inference from reading the code; I did not run the tests against the base commit.

findings.summary: I could not confirm that the retry chain is what actually lost the correction in hrdp/9e8t.
findings.evidence: There are no records in the workspace (a search for "9e8t" found nothing), so I could not check whether 9e8t was itself a retry. The fix matches the reading's main suspect, and the reader brief already handled failed jobs.

findings.summary: Two of the expected deliverables were not changed: lifecycle.rs and store.rs.
findings.evidence: The diff stat lists only CHANGELOG.md, briefs.rs and reading.rs. No acceptance criterion requires those files, and the small default favours a narrow change.

summary: The change passes all five criteria; I found nothing blocking. When the user retries a job that was itself a retry, Athena now walks back through the chain of retried jobs. It carries their accepted corrections, oldest first, ahead of the failed job's own, and redacts them. This covers the likely cause of the dropped correction: the old code carried only the original request through the chain, not the corrections. Because the code is shared, rejected-job retries get the same treatment. There are new tests for a failed job's own corrections being kept in order and redacted, for a failed job with no verification record, for a failed retry chain, and for the reader brief listing corrections under the existing heading. All of them pass. I ran the full `cargo test` and it passed, and clippy and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. Three small points: two of the new reading tests probably pass on the old code too, so only the chain test reproduces the bug; I could not confirm against the hrdp/9e8t records that a retry chain was the real cause, because no records are in the workspace; and lifecycle.rs and store.rs, listed as expected deliverables, were not changed.
